item: Low-memory path for encrypted merges: identity groupings in an encrypted scratch file
summary: R319 release note: imports into an encrypted corpus on machines with little free memory no longer need the duplicate-grouping steps to fit in RAM; when they do not, the groupings run in a scratch file next to the data, encrypted with the corpus key and deleted afterwards, instead of the import being refused (measured: 197 MB instead of 351 MB extra memory on 6 million incoming keywords, same speed). The id maps still need about 16 bytes per incoming row.
